Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Possible personal/family history of autoimmune illness (father) may increase health vigilance; high activity/work demands.
- Precipitating factors: Onset of neurological symptoms (left arm numbness/tingling, transient visual disturbance) following viral illness and increased physical activity (boxing).
- Perpetuating factors: Ongoing neurological symptoms affecting daily activities (exercise, piano) and uncertainty pending specialist assessment; online health searches; fatigue.
- Protective factors: Engagement with healthcare; willingness to follow up; existing social network; baseline healthy lifestyle.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce worry and manage stress while awaiting neurological evaluation
  - Maintain function in daily activities and sleep as able
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Screen for anxiety and depressive symptoms and monitor distress during diagnostic process
  - Provide brief, skills-based support for coping with uncertainty and symptom-related stress
- Actions (Patient):
  - Use structured worry time and limit unhelpful online searching to ≤30 minutes/day
  - Practice daily relaxation (e.g., diaphragmatic breathing, progressive muscle relaxation) 10–15 minutes
  - Maintain routine (sleep/wake times, light physical activity within medical guidance)
  - Track mood, sleep, and worry triggers in a brief log
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Administer GAD-7 and PHQ-9 at next contact; repeat in 2–4 weeks
  - Provide psychoeducation on coping with health-related uncertainty and stress
  - Offer brief CBT-informed strategies or refer to counseling/psychology for short-term support
  - Coordinate with Neurology regarding referral and update patient on timelines

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Improve sleep consistency without over-reliance on melatonin
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Enhance sleep hygiene; monitor frequency and efficacy of melatonin use
- Actions (Patient):
  - Implement sleep hygiene: consistent schedule, reduce late caffeine/alcohol, wind-down routine, limit screens 1 hour before bed
  - Use melatonin only as needed; record usage and perceived benefit
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide written sleep hygiene guidance
  - Review melatonin use and consider non-pharmacologic sleep interventions first

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Not recorded. Topics Covered: Not recorded
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Escalating anxiety interfering with work/sleep
  - Persistent rumination, panic symptoms, or avoidance of activities
- Coping Strategies:
  - Brief relaxation practices, scheduled problem-solving, structured support from trusted contacts
  - Maintain balanced activity pacing per medical guidance

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- No mental health-related differential diagnoses were provided in the DDx. The DDx focuses on neurological conditions (e.g., cervical radiculopathy, median nerve entrapment, multiple sclerosis). No mental health differentials documented; none added to avoid speculation.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Formal psychiatric diagnosis; standardized screening results (PHQ-9/GAD-7); complete MSE; suicide risk assessment and overall risk level; living situation; substance use (smoking/other); consent and review date; emergency contact.  
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: DDx references “female” demographics; gender not explicitly recorded in transcript. Otherwise consistent.  
● Transcript quality notes: Some dialogue interruptions and minor ambiguities (brief confusion about neck pain); no formal mental health review conducted; primarily neurological consultation.
